analyst_view.overall: Parma (16th, 8 points, one win in their last six and beaten in the derby at Bologna) host Roma (3rd, 27 points, two off the top after a 3-0 win over Sassuolo and 21 goals in their last six). Gilardino's back line is stretched: Ndiaye is suspended and Romero out until after Christmas (both in the numbers), while Diego Carlos (thigh/adductor strain) is in serious doubt and Bernabé is still out; Drobnic's foot problem looks to have cleared, as Virgilio and Fantamaster both put him in the back three. Gasperini confirmed on Friday that Dybala and Svilar are recovered and can start, with only Pellegrini and Rensch missing (counted); Koné may be managed and Dybala and Soulé could share the minutes. Referee Simone Sozza (4.2 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already take Romero off Parma (-14%) and lift Roma for their scoring run. What they can't see is a Parma back three most likely without Diego Carlos, their most experienced defender, against a Roma attack getting Dybala back; Gasperini called Gilardino's sides compact, so I keep only a mild lean up to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add Roma's strong recent corner count (+9%). Roma's wing-backs Molina and Wesley push high and Parma will likely sit deep, but that pattern is already in Roma's recent figures, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add Sozza's above-average record (4.2 a game, +13%). There is no rivalry here and Roma have been fairly clean lately (already counted); Parma's makeshift defence may have to foul more, but not enough for me to move, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already raised a lot for Roma's recent shooting (+26%). A weakened Parma defence points up, but Roma may manage Koné and split Dybala's and Soulé's minutes, and the figure is already high, so I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target and already lift Roma for their recent accuracy (+13%). Dybala, confirmed fit by Gasperini, adds finishing quality the recent games lacked, against a Parma line probably missing Diego Carlos as well as Ndiaye; a small nudge to about 9.7.
